text:
Maya: heads-up — we saw a handful of tiny customers get auto-fallbacked last night due to a single outlier latency spike in the region. Noticed in rollout c-204 canary. :grimacing:
Aj: hmm. Is this the 'sparse-trigger' case where a single error flips the policy? We currently use a 10s eval window and sample audit 0.1%. That could over-index small buckets.
Sophia: can we add a minimum_requests threshold so we don't make deterministic decisions on n < 10 requests? e.g., require at least 5 failures or a computed confidence score before opening fallback.
Maya: yes that's the ask. Also ops were spammed because each fallback generated a separate operator inbox item — very noisy.
Nate: thinking: two-pronged change: 1) debounce per-route per-customer with exponential backoff; 2) aggregate audit events into a single grouped inbox item with an incident_bucket id so duplicates collapse. Also add a sticky override TTL.
Aj: rough config sketch:```json
{
  "fallback": {
    "trigger": "error_rate",
    "min_requests": 10,
    "window_secs": 30,
    "debounce_secs": 300,
    "audit_sample": 0.02,
    "group_inbox_by": "policy_id"
  }
}
```This keeps small tenants from getting tripped by single anomalies.
Liam: we also need telemetry fields: emit decision_confidence and sampled_payload_id so we can replay decisions for evals. Ops wants ability to replay the last 5 artifacts tied to a group.
Sophia: agree. But watch quotas — if we increase sampling or store full payloads we'll blow up logging/egress. Proposal: store minimal snapshot (reason_code + summary stats + link to on-demand payload store). Payload store is cold by default.
Maya: yep, prefer that. Snapshot should be tiny: reason_code, counts, moving_average_latency, and a payload_s3_key (nullable).
OpsBot: deploy/canary finished for branch autofallback-sparse-fix 1779993210 — canary=20% :white_check_mark:
Aj: thanks @OpsBot. UX ask: console should show "fallback events (grouped)" with a grouped timeline and a waterfall showing the causal signals (latency, 5xx, model OOM). Operator affordances: 'silence customer' + 'sticky override 1h' + quick link to replay snapshot.
Nate: edge-case: if min_requests=10, truly tiny customers may never get protection even during a real outage. Counter-proposal: symmetric rule where for small customers we allow fallback if absolute_errors > 0 AND severity >= 2 (e.g., http 5xx or model OOM), but those always create a manual-review flag (requires operator ack).
Maya: sounds reasonable. Add runbook step for manual-review flow and who gets pinged.
Sophia: I'll draft runbook and telemetry schema. Aj — can you put up a config + telemetry PR? Also add unit tests for the grouping/debounce logic.
Aj: will do. PR: https://git.company/repo/pull/8123 (includes config + telemetry + inbox grouping). Reviewers: @Maya @Nate.
Maya: one more: add a metric to the quota dashboard called fallback_noisy_customers (count of grouped fallbacks where group_size <= threshold) so product can signal to CSMs.
Liam: I'll add chart to the console. :thumbsup:
Nate: quick note — make sure grouping key is stable across restarts (use policy_id + route + customer_id hashed). Otherwise inbox dedupe will fail.
Aj: good catch. We'll persist group_id in the audit event.
Maya: great. Thanks team — follow-ups: Sophia runbook by EOD, Aj PR within today, Ops will monitor canary noise.
Sophia: on it.
Liam: monitoring alert rule added: eng.platform.autofallback.noisy_group_rate > 1 => pager suppressed but slack notify.
Maya: perfect.
